meta.note: Sources collected from the IANPHI tools page, the US CDC SDT page and a literature search. One-line takeaways are in our own words, based on the page or abstract that was read, not full texts. Items marked as not read were listed from titles only.

sources.title: Addressing emerging public health threats: the Noncommunicable Disease Capacity Assessment and Planning (N-CAP) Process
sources.authors: Saad RK, Alsouri R, Kruse MH, Kufoof L, Lobanov-Rostovsky S, Richter P, Khader Y
sources.takeaway: The N-CAP adapts the SDT for NCDs: stakeholder mapping, a SWOT workshop and a multi-day guide-based workshop. Jordan (2021) focused on the data-to-action continuum and fed into its NCD strategy; Iraq (2022) used the coalition guide and strengthened its NCD coalition; early ministry involvement and local facilitators mattered.

sources.title: Staged Development Tool (SDT) case study: Colombia Instituto Nacional de Salud, implementation and outcomes
sources.takeaway: Nine guides used in week-long workshops in 2017, with outside Spanish-speaking facilitators; over 100 activities prioritised by importance, feasibility and urgency; plans used for funding requests; strong director backing and mandatory attendance of key staff; progress re-assessed in 2018 and 2019.
sources.note: Publication year not stated; workshops were held in April and July 2017 with an earlier version of the guides.

sources.title: Best practice guidance: legal mandates and governance of national public health institutes
sources.takeaway: Make the mandate and the degree of autonomy within the ministry explicit; compare line agency, parastatal and hybrid models; protect scientific independence; plan the transition, because renaming a unit rarely works; full capacity often takes decades.

sources.title: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control: legal framework case study
sources.takeaway: Created in 2011 and made a parastatal by the 2018 law after the Ebola outbreak showed the need; it began working before the law passed, which built support; leaving structure details out of the law keeps them easy to change; backing by the minister and the president helped.
sources.note: Year is approximate.

sources.title: IANPHI peer review of Public Health England: evaluation and recommendations
sources.takeaway: Eight-member team, four days on site, using the IANPHI framework and evaluation tool. PHE merged 129 bodies in under five years and cut costs by about 30%. Advice: allocate resources by burden and preventability, make emergency communications resilient, share the change story through IANPHI.

sources.title: NPHI development in Africa, status February 2023
sources.takeaway: A desk review of 55 member states found 19 with an established NPHI and 21 in process. Only 9 of the 19 had a current strategic plan, and government funding covered 40% of budgets on average (range 1% to 95%). Recommendations: review public health laws first, secure political buy-in, find a national champion, use peer exchange.
sources.note: Figures from slides; the legal-framework table in the source is not fully consistent.

sources.title: Lessons learned from national public health institutes' response to the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020
sources.authors: Rigal L, Desenclos JC, Sandifer Q (IANPHI)
sources.takeaway: Clear mandates and communication lines before a crisis, multisectoral partnerships, workforce strain, adapted preparedness. Examples: Colombia grew PCR testing from about 200 to nearly 64,000 tests a day; Peru went from one to 64 laboratories; Wales opened a sampling centre in under three days; RIVM used behavioural science.
